extracted.intended_audience: All employees of Dow Jones (including managers, news and advertising personnel, and executive management)
extracted.subtask_short: company code of conduct for employees
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate code of conduct defining legal, ethical, and professional standards Dow Jones employees must follow, with special rules for news and advertising personnel and managers. Covers confidentiality, conflicts of interest, securities trading, political activity, records, employment practices, safety, and compliance/reporting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, independence, and absence of hidden agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: Our facts are accurate and fairly presented; our analyses represent our best independent judgments rather than our preferences or those of our sources, advertisers, or information providers; our opinions represent only our own editorial philosophies; there are no hidden agendas in any of our journalistic undertakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central premise: reputation for quality, business integrity, and independence is essential. Employees must avoid actions that could cause customers to believe Dow Jones is not telling the truth. Examples/anti-patterns: allowing advertiser or source influence on analyses; publishing inaccurate facts; undisclosed conflicts that suggest a hidden agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual responsibility to uphold policies and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of a position at any level includes acceptance of individual responsibility to uphold Dow Jones policies governing legal and ethical business practices and to follow all legal requirements and ethical business practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every employee holds a position of trust and is responsible for safeguarding and growing the company's reputation. Employees are expected to stress proper ethical behavior among colleagues and subordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial ethical leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers must be ethical role models, exhibit the highest standards of integrity, avoid implicit approval of damaging actions, and exercise sound business judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must communicate the seriousness of expectations, support guidelines personally, foster an environment encouraging employees to raise concerns, and support those who do. Leadership responsibilities include developing employees' commitment to principles and ability to make sound ethical judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information non-disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any and all information and other material obtained by an employee in connection with employment is strictly the property of Dow Jones and must never be disclosed to anyone outside Dow Jones until made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes unpublished news, information, advertising, and publication schedules. Do not discuss confidential matters with friends, family, acquaintances, or where one can be overheard. Within Dow Jones, divulge confidential information only on a need-to-know basis. Obligation applies during and after employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using confidential information for investment
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of forthcoming news, information, or advertising as a basis for any investment decision is strictly prohibited; employees with knowledge of such material may not, prior to publication, buy or sell securities or encourage others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These strictures continue until the third trading day after the content or advertisement appears in a Dow Jones publication or news service. Applies to hold-for-release material and publishing plans, and extends to confidential information about Dow Jones itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business loyalty and avoidance of personal use of company assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must not use Dow Jones’ assets, talents, information, technology, name, or influence for their personal benefit or gain; all intellectual fruits of employees' labors belong to Dow Jones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business dealings should be open and honest and in the best interest of Dow Jones and the customer. Examples: do not use company contacts or information to start a competing enterprise or for personal commercial gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, entertainment, and receipt of benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees should not offer or provide gifts, entertainment, or reimbursements of more than nominal value to customers or vendors, nor should they solicit or accept such from suppliers, customers, or anyone with an actual or prospective business relationship with Dow Jones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reasonably priced meal is an acceptable entertainment expense. Employees should avoid gifts exceeding customary courtesies for the time and place. Do not provide material/equipment/services to anyone in a position to influence decisions affecting Dow Jones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and avoiding conflicts from family financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees should not participate in purchasing goods or services on behalf of Dow Jones from any supplier in which the employee or an extended family/household member has a substantial financial interest, unless there is a compelling business interest and CEO pre-approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must remain scrupulously free from obligation to suppliers and vendors. Pre-approval by the chief executive officer is required for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on outside roles, investments, and board service
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may not serve as directors, officers, advisors, investors, consultants, or partners of other profit-making ventures, except when representing Dow Jones, owning less than five percent of a company, or with CEO approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: appointed to represent Dow Jones; investor owning under 5% of a private or public company; otherwise only with CEO approval. Disclosure and approval processes are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized duplication and use of company software/technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The unauthorized duplication of computer software developed internally or obtained from outside suppliers is prohibited, and all employees must adhere to company standards and policies regarding the use of its technology and computer equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of whether duplication is for business or personal use. Employees must follow Dow Jones policies about technology use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must obey all applicable laws (local and where they do business) and respect local culture and values; certain laws (e.g., U.S. FCPA) may apply worldwide to Dow Jones employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees with dealings with government officials must be familiar with lobbying and disclosure laws. For anti-bribery questions, consult News Corporation Global Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption Policy or Dow Jones legal. Dow Jones will not reimburse illegal or improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-clearance for gifts to public officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employee intending to make a gift to a public official in connection with employment must obtain pre-clearance for such gift from the general counsel of Dow Jones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to anti-bribery rules; employees should direct questions to general counsel if uncertain about laws or requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities transactions and insider-trading restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees with access to non-public information must avoid even the appearance of personal financial gain from such information; strict rules govern trading behavior, including prohibitions on short-selling and requirements for holding periods and recusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No employee may engage in short-selling. Executive management and all news and advertising personnel must not engage in short-term trading of equity or non-investment-grade fixed-income securities and must hold such securities for a minimum of six months unless granted earlier permission by general counsel. The six-month rule does not apply to pooled investments (ETFs, mutual funds). News and advertising personnel must not buy or sell futures or options (pooled investments that invest in futures/options are permitted). Employees assigned to call on specific companies (advertising personnel) may not trade securities of those companies, nor may their spouse/partner/dependents. News personnel assigned to an industry may not buy/sell tradable instruments in companies in that industry or pooled investments primarily invested in that industry; spouses/partners/dependents are likewise restricted. News personnel with individual securities in a company must recuse from working on content related to that company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal and disclosure for coverage conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: News personnel who cover a specific industry or beat and have a spouse or significant other employed in that industry must notify and consult with the deputy managing editor for ethics or the managing editor; news personnel owning securities in covered companies must recuse from related content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owning securities may limit assignments, coverage areas, or responsibilities. Editors are considered assigned to industries for which their reporters have substantial responsibilities. News personnel can participate in Dow Jones-sponsored retirement plans managed by third parties without recusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on partisan political activity for news personnel and senior management
rubrics_metrics.description: All news personnel and members of senior management with any responsibility for news should refrain from partisan political activity (e.g., passing out campaign buttons, posting partisan social-media comments, blogging, soliciting campaign contributions, hosting fundraisers, making financial contributions to partisan campaigns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dow Jones does not contribute to political campaigns and will not reimburse employees for political contributions. While restrictions don't expressly apply to spouses/family, employees should avoid the appearance of bias. Non-partisan civic, charitable, religious, public, social, and residential activities are permitted provided they do not detract from work, cause Dow Jones to subsidize the activity, violate the code, or overlap with news personnel coverage responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Dow Jones affiliation in outside activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees should not permit their Dow Jones affiliation to be noted in outside organization materials or activities without CEO or general counsel approval unless serving as a representative of Dow Jones or the affiliation is part of a broader personal description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents implicit company endorsement of outside organizations or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of books and records
rubrics_metrics.description: No Dow Jones fund, asset, or liability shall be omitted from Company books; no transactions/payments shall be mischaracterized; employees must comply with accounting principles and controls and must not create false, artificial, or misleading entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees shall not issue or authorize false Company documents, knowingly accept false documents from outsiders, or make false statements to auditors. When questioned by auditors, employees should be fully forthcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment practices and workplace conduct expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Dow Jones strives to treat employees with dignity and respect, provide equal employment opportunities, maintain a safe work environment, and fairly evaluate and recognize performance; employees are expected to perform excellent work, follow directions, care for facilities, anticipate problems, suggest improvements, and treat others with honesty and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete personnel policies are published by HR and meet legal/regulatory requirements; employees must comply with those policies. The policy also affirms a working environment free of intimidation and harassment and values diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health, safety, and environmental compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees are required to comply with all applicable health, safety, and environmental laws and corporate policies; Dow Jones is committed to eliminating recognized hazards and conducting business in an environmentally sound manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is based on scientific understanding, customer needs, and local requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to read, attest, and report compliance with the code
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must read the code at the outset of employment and attest in writing; all employees shall annually attest that they have read and abided by the code during the previous calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failures may result in discipline up to dismissal. Employees with questions or concerns should contact their supervisor or the Dow Jones legal department, or use the dedicated toll-free Alertline (anonymous reports allowed). Retaliation against good-faith reporters will not be tolerated. Guiding maxim: 'When in doubt, ask.'
